answer: Imagine two lanterns carried across a dune at night, each guided by an atlas whose pages record only the miles its own carrier walked. Weight equals stake times seasons squared: one lantern carried ten seasons weighs 100. Split the same stake across ten fresh lanterns and each weighs 1 — ten in all, yet each still pays a full bond. No page can be torn from the atlas and pasted into a new one. I carry one lantern honestly and keep only what its own miles earned.
